chains.title: CTCF binding hypothesis
chains.element: The variant is outside an annotated cCRE, and no element activity or cCRE-to-gene link is available for this site.

links.claim: The F1 in-vitro binding screen reports greater binding of the alternate T allele; CTCF is the named family member, but its ChIP-seq peak is elsewhere.

critique.reason: E12 reports greater in-vitro binding for the alternate allele, and E13 identifies CTCF as the named F1 member. Under the stated rule, the QBiC-SELEX model counts as CTCF's own model; the peak elsewhere limits evidence for occupancy in MCF7, not for the model's binding prediction.

regrade.reason: E12–E13 report greater in-vitro binding for the alternate allele and name CTCF, but this is a binding screen rather than evidence of in-cell occupancy or function.

links.claim: No cCRE overlaps the variant, so the evidence does not establish a regulatory element at this position.

critique.reason: E03 and E05 report that no annotated cCRE overlaps the variant. This supports the claim that the supplied evidence does not establish a regulatory element here; it does not prove that no functional element exists.

regrade.reason: E03 and E05 show that the variant does not overlap an annotated cCRE; E06 reports no cCRE-gene link. This supports the claim that the supplied evidence does not establish a regulatory element here.

links.claim: The only gene-specific lead is a low-PIP brain-nucleus eQTL for ENSG00000259868; GTEx v8 found no significant single-tissue eQTL. The evidence does not provide an HGNC symbol for this Ensembl ID or establish it as the target in MCF7.

critique.reason: E08 reports only a low-PIP eQTL for ENSG00000259868 in brain nucleus accumbens, and E09 reports no significant GTEx v8 single-tissue eQTL. These results do not establish this gene as the target in MCF7.

regrade.reason: E08 provides only a low-PIP eQTL for ENSG00000259868 in brain, and E09 reports no significant GTEx v8 eQTL. These are indirect and do not establish this gene as the target in MCF7. E15 failed and adds no evidence.

links.claim: CTCF is expressed in the stated MCF7 context, but the supplied CTCF ChIP-seq peak is from other cell lines, not MCF7.

critique.reason: E13 reports CTCF expression in the MCF7 context. E12 reports no matched-biosample ChIP-seq peak near the variant and says the observed peak is elsewhere, so the evidence supports expression but not local CTCF occupancy in MCF7.

regrade.reason: E13 reports CTCF expression in MCF7, while E14 directly reports no CTCF ChIP-seq peak overlapping the variant in MCF7. This supports the stated distinction between expression and occupancy evidence.

links.claim: The supplied evidence does not establish an association with breast cancer; the variant has no listed GWAS association, and the intake reports no disease association.

critique.reason: E07 and E10 provide no listed breast-cancer association for the variant. This supports the cautious claim that the supplied evidence does not establish a phenotype link, not a claim that the variant has no effect.

regrade.reason: E07 and E10 report no listed breast-cancer association, supporting the claim that the supplied evidence does not establish a phenotype link. E15 is a failed lookup and does not change this assessment.

predictions: The T allele should show greater CTCF binding than C in an allele-comparative binding assay; if this hypothesis is functional in MCF7, allele-specific CTCF occupancy should also favor T.
falsified_if: A suitably powered allele-comparative assay fails to reproduce greater CTCF binding to T.
In MCF7, allele-specific occupancy or perturbation tests show no CTCF-dependent regulatory effect at the variant.

problems: The alternate-allele CTCF result is in vitro only; E14 provides tested-negative evidence for CTCF occupancy at the variant in MCF7.
No regulatory element or cCRE-to-gene link is established at the variant, and the low-PIP brain eQTL does not establish ENSG00000259868 as the target in MCF7.
No breast-cancer association is established by the supplied evidence. The failed E15 lookup provides no additional evidence.

checks.why: A CTCF ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF7 would add direct evidence of local occupancy; its absence would leave the in-vitro binding prediction unvalidated in the stated cell context.
A gene-level breast-cancer association could add context for the proposed target, although it would not establish that this variant regulates the gene.

critique.next_experiment: Test the C/T alleles in a validated allele-comparative CTCF binding assay, then assess allele-specific CTCF occupancy and regulatory effect in MCF7; the negative ChIP-seq result makes the in-cell follow-up especially important.

lookups.why: A CTCF ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF7 would add direct evidence of local occupancy; its absence would leave the in-vitro binding prediction unvalidated in the stated cell context.
